        self, console: "Console", options: "ConsoleOptions"
    ) -> Iterable[Segment]:
        tab_size: int = console.tab_size if self.tab_size is None else self.tab_size
        justify = self.justify or options.justify or DEFAULT_JUSTIFY
        overflow = self.overflow or options.overflow or DEFAULT_OVERFLOW

        lines = self.wrap(
            console,
            options.max_width,
            justify=justify,
            overflow=overflow,
            tab_size=tab_size or 8,
            no_wrap=pick_bool(self.no_wrap, options.no_wrap, False),
        )
        all_lines = Text("\n").join(lines)
        yield from all_lines.render(console, end=self.end)

    def __rich_measure__(
        self, console: "Console", options: "ConsoleOptions"

        text = self.plain
        lines = text.splitlines()

        words = text.split()
        min_text_width = (
            max(cell_len(word) for word in words) if words else max_text_width
        )
        return Measurement(min_text_width, max_text_width)

I changed `rich/console.py` so that, with `soft_wrap=True` and a `style` argument, styled text is split on newlines and each line is styled separately. I did not confirm that this is the exact behaviour from issue #3838, and the hidden tests were not run.

I reproduced a difference: `print('hello\nworld', style='on red', soft_wrap=True)` put the newline inside one styled segment, while the wrapped path styled each line on its own. The fix adds a `_split_segments_on_newline` helper and applies it in `Console.print` only when `soft_wrap` is set. One side effect: the newline segment now carries the style too, which differs from the wrapped path, where newlines are unstyled. The existing console tests matching `soft`, `style` or `print` pass (19 selected).
